text.p: Amgen Inc expects to report 1996 earnings of between $2.35 and $2.42 a share on revenues of more than $2.0 billion, the company said Thursday at the Hambrecht & Quist healthcare conference here.
In 1995 the company earned $1.92 a share on revenues of $1.94 billion.
The company said two lead products, Epogen and Neupogen, will each contribute in excess of $1.0 billion to revenues.

It said Neupogen sales have grown less rapidly than Epogen in recent months due partly to a competing drug introduced by Rhone-Poulenc in Europe. Chief Financial Officer Bob Attiyeah said Neupogen has held onto 75 percent of the European market in the face of stiff competition.

Attiyeah said Infergen will most likely be the next Amgen product to come on the market. Infergen, a drug to treat Hepatitis C, is expected to get U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval in the first half of 1997, he said.
Neupogen is a drug widely used in cancer chemotherapy treatment while Epogen is used patients with kidney disease.
